transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-09-14
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~55 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Miles (Redwood AE), Priya Kapoor (Redwood SE), Liam O'Neill (Arcturus Head of ML), Sofia Chen (Arcturus Platform Eng), Marcus Rivera (Arcturus CTO)

Summary (auto): Quick run through of Arcturus production traffic patterns, define POC success metrics, and agree on benchmark plan.

[00:00:00] Jordan Miles: hey everyone, thanks for joining, um we wanted to focus today on the workload modelling piece and make sure we can scope the POC tests properly
[00:00:08] Liam O'Neill: yeah thanks Jordan, appreciate it. we are mainly interested in two things: latency under steady-state and cost per transaction, and also how the system behaves under spikes
[00:00:16] Priya Kapoor: great, can you give us a bit more context on current qps and concurrency? rough numbers are fine
[00:00:22] Sofia Chen: sure. normal traffic is about 60 qps globally, peaks at around 220 qps during settlement windows. concurrency wise we see roughly 120 concurrent user sessions hitting our inference endpoints during peaks but that maps to about 180 active requests because of async workflows
[00:00:38] Marcus Rivera: also note some endpoints are heavier: report generation calls produce long outputs, 400-800 tokens sometimes
[00:00:45] Jordan Miles: ok good, that's helpful. when you say 400-800 tokens is that output length or total (input+output)?
[00:00:50] Marcus Rivera: mostly output; inputs are shorter, usually 30-80 tokens (customers ask for context + instructions)
[00:00:55] Priya Kapoor: got it. so rough distribution: input median ~60, output median ~120 but tail up to 800 for a small percent of calls. that drives sequence length planning for kernels and kv cache sizing
[00:01:10] Liam O'Neill: yeah about 5-7% of requests are those long reports; majority are short 1-2 turn flows where output tokens are ~40-150
[00:01:20] Jordan Miles: perfect. for the POC we usually suggest modelling three traffic profiles: nominal (50-80 qps), peak (200-250 qps), and spike (burst to 400 qps for 1-5 minutes). does that align with what you see?
[00:01:31] Sofia Chen: yes that matches. our SLA target is p95 latency under 300ms for the short flows. the long report flows are allowed higher latency up to 2s p95 but we'd prefer less
[00:01:44] Priya Kapoor: ok we should capture separate SLOs per request class then. success criteria from our side to demonstrate value: p95 < 300ms for short flows at peak, throughput sustainment at 200 qps for 30 minutes without error rate increase, and cost per 1M tokens below your threshold; we'll need target number from you
[00:02:01] Liam O'Neill: cost target is roughly $4-5 per 1M tokens equivalent (we have internal benchmarks), but that's flexible if latency wins out
[00:02:10] Jordan Miles: noted. we'll run the POC on a mirrored workload and give you both hosted and dedicated cost estimates with quantized runtimes included
[00:02:18] Marcus Rivera: security question: data residency and logs. we need audit logs and that data stays in our VPC, can Redwood's private deployment option work for the POC or do you need hosted?
[00:02:28] Priya Kapoor: for initial benchmarking we often run in our hosted infra for speed, but we can run a dedicated instance provisioned in your VPC (Private) for the security tests. for the POC phase we can do the throughput tests in hosted to iterate quickly, then re-run the critical workloads in a private/Dedicated environment to validate network and KMS integration
[00:02:45] Sofia Chen: that sounds reasonable. for the Dedicated test we will need SSO and the KMS integration tested, plus a proof of audit log delivery into our SIEM
[00:02:54] Jordan Miles: understood. Priya, from a technical bench perspective, what telemetry do you need?
[00:02:58] Priya Kapoor: ideally: 1) raw request traces (timestamp, input len, output len, latency), 2) QPS by endpoint, 3) error rates and stack traces for failures, 4) resource utilization (GPU, CPU, memory) per host. if you can provide a 7-day sample of your traffic traces we can synthesize a realistic replay.
[00:03:16] Liam O'Neill: we can do that; we'll scrub PII and send by next week.
[00:03:20] Jordan Miles: great. on the modelling side, we plan to run three benchmarks: latency SLO test at 200 qps, throughput ramp test up to 400 qps to find saturation, and long-tail correctness/quality check with a sample set of 2k prompts. any additions?
[00:03:33] Marcus Rivera: can you include fallback behavior tests? like when a GPU pool is constrained, auto-routing to a lower-capacity quantized model and measure degradation in latency/quality
[00:03:40] Priya Kapoor: yes we can simulate routing policies: can do canary and fallback scenarios, and we can quantify quality regression via the 2k prompt evals (we'll run automatic evals comparing outputs to your golden set)
[00:03:55] Sofia Chen: about tokenization differences: we use a custom tokenizer wrapper, sometimes token counts in our logs look off by 10-15% compared to off-the-shelf tokenizers
[00:04:02] Priya Kapoor: good to know; we'll ask you to include both raw strings and tokenized counts so we can reconcile and ensure kernel sizing is accurate
[00:04:10] Jordan Miles: timeline wise, if we get logs by 2027-09-21, Priya can deliver initial hosted benchmark runs by 2027-09-28 and then Dedicated validation in the following week. decision review meeting target 2027-10-05. does that work?
[00:04:21] Liam O'Neill: that timeline is fine.
[00:04:23] Marcus Rivera: yes, but one caveat: we have an internal compliance freeze the week of 2027-09-26 so any infra changes need to be completed before then for the Dedicated test to be provisioned quickly
[00:04:33] Jordan Miles: ok, we'll try to prioritize the Dedicated setup earlier if needed.
[00:04:36] Priya Kapoor: technical notes on the modelling: we will capture qps as poisson arrivals in the replay with burst windows to match your settlement spikes. concurrency we model at the application layer; for longer outputs we'll model both streaming and non-streaming variants to capture tail latency differences
[00:04:53] Sofia Chen: streaming is important for the UX of long reports; if streaming reduces p95 that's preferable, so include it in the test matrix
[00:04:59] Priya Kapoor: will do. also we'll include batching studies to show throughput vs latency tradeoffs at different batch sizes and quantization profiles (int8, ggml-style quantized variants)
[00:05:09] Liam O'Neill: what's your suggested test sizes? like number of iterations or synthetic users?
[00:05:13] Priya Kapoor: for statistical significance: at least 30 minutes steady-state per profile, with a 10-minute ramp and 5-minute spike windows. for the 2k prompt evals we'll run multiple seeds and aggregate quality metrics (BLEU/ROUGE not perfect for your domain but we'll use domain-specific heuristics and human checks for a subset)
[00:05:29] Jordan Miles: success criteria recap: 1) short flows p95 < 300ms at peak 200 qps, 2) throughput sustain at 200 qps for 30 minutes with error rate <0.1%, 3) quality regression vs your golden set <5% for short flows, long report f1/qual metrics acceptable to you, 4) security checklist satisfied for Dedicated test.
[00:05:45] Marcus Rivera: yes and add cost guidance: if you can show Dedicated cost per 1M tokens below $6 with our quantization profile that would be compelling
[00:05:54] Jordan Miles: we'll include cost scenarios (hosted vs dedicated) and show unit economics with batching and caching assumptions. we'll also show how prefix/kvcache can reduce repeated token costs for conversational sessions
[00:06:06] Sofia Chen: one more operational ask: can you provide observability hooks? we use Datadog and Splunk; hope you can ship traces and metrics there
[00:06:12] Priya Kapoor: yes Redwood Console supports exporting Prometheus metrics and log delivery to your SIEM, we'll include instructions in the security pack
[00:06:20] Liam O'Neill: ok great. are there any blockers you see on your side?
[00:06:24] Priya Kapoor: just the traffic traces and a couple test accounts to hit non-prod endpoints. ideally a small allowlist of source IPs for Dedicated provisioning
[00:06:32] Jordan Miles: to be explicit on deliverables: Priya will run the hosted benchmark and share results + raw telemetry; we'll then schedule Dedicated validation and security integration tests. follow-up meeting to review results and make a go/no-go decision on the pilot on 2027-10-05.
[00:06:46] Marcus Rivera: sounds good. one last question: what's the bench hardware you use for hosted runs? GPUs? which family?
[00:06:51] Priya Kapoor: for hosted we use a mix of A100 and H100 families depending on model size; for quantized variants we run on cost-optimized nodes (A10G or comparable) to show realistic economics. we'll annotate every result with hardware used
[00:07:03] Jordan Miles: perfect. any other questions?
[00:07:06] Sofia Chen: not from me.
[00:07:07] Liam O'Neill: none here. thanks, appreciate the clarity.
[00:07:10] Jordan Miles: ok we'll follow up with the benchmark harness and the action items. thanks everyone.
